factual_methodological.summary: Material current macro claims were rechecked against primary sources: TurkStat reports August 2026 CPI at 31.51%, Q2 2026 real GDP growth at 2.3% year on year and August unemployment at 7.8%; CBRT kept the one-week repo policy rate at 37%. Observed data, institutional claims, forecasts and scenarios remain distinguished.

editorial_publication_readiness.summary: The opening states the industrial-scale/disinflation/strategic-autonomy thesis directly; headings identify mechanisms rather than template fields; EN and PT-BR read as localized institutional prose; the argument progresses through institutional history, macro stabilisation, labour/demography, productive structure, energy, security and social transmission to scenarios and falsifiers without exposing QA or prompt structure.

contextual_depth.summary: Ottoman/republican path dependence, post-1980 liberalisation, the 2001 institutional break, EU Customs Union, executive architecture, migration, regional inequality, security and energy geography are incorporated where they explain current capabilities and constraints rather than as ornamental chronology.

visual_evidence_readiness.signature: evidence-bearing geographic map + multiple explicit charts + causal flows + mind map + contradiction table in each locale
visual_evidence_readiness.summary: Revision 1 resolves the prior visual blocker with a bilingual map covering EU manufacturing linkage, the Turkish Straits, Black Sea, Caucasus, Middle East and Eastern Mediterranean. It explicitly qualifies the map as functional exposure rather than precise routes or quantitative flows. Quantitative and structural visuals are semantically aligned across EN/PT-BR.

country_context_contract.summary: The item is explicitly country-level, uses context_role country-context and country-dossier format, and links Turkish macro, industrial, energy, migration and security mechanisms to canonical Europe-Russia-Ukraine, Russia, Iran and Saudi research rather than presenting an encyclopedic profile.

political_neutrality.summary: Executive structure, security relationships, refugee policy and the Kurdish question are described with attribution and observable institutional distinctions; legal political/civil categories are separated from armed organisations and official policy claims are not treated as independent proof of effectiveness.

contrary_evidence: Inflation above 30% and recurring lira volatility coexist with low sovereign debt, functioning banks, manufacturing exports and tourism receipts, arguing against an institutional-collapse interpretation.
EU accession negotiations remain stalled while the Customs Union and goods supply chains preserve deep commercial integration.
Domestic gas, LNG optionality and renewables improve resilience while natural-gas import dependence remains very high, so diversification is not energy autarky.

Defence exports demonstrate substantial industrial capability but do not establish full technological autonomy or domestic value added because imported components, certification and external technology remain relevant.
limitations: Inflation and growth forecasts changed materially during 2026 and are kept attributed to their forecast vintages rather than averaged.
Turkish official sources are primary for administrative, trade, energy and defence quantities but are not independent evaluations of policy performance.
Refugee stocks change through registration, return, resettlement and status changes; the cited UNHCR headline is a dated stock rather than a fixed 2026 population.
Ethnicity is not comprehensively measured in official statistics, so no unsupported ethnic population shares are assigned.
Defence-export values are not equivalent to domestic value added, operational effectiveness or independently verified technological content.
Akkuyu first-unit generation was not treated as realised supply at the evidence cutoff.
The geographic map encodes functional exposure and transmission, not precise routes, capacities or flow volumes.
notes: Approved after re-review of changed revision-1 pending/source SHAs. The prior blocking issue is resolved by an evidence-bearing bilingual geographic map. Current public state was re-read immediately before the decision and contained no public Türkiye bundle for this ID. Revision 1 is therefore a new-item QA revision, not a revision of an already materialized public bundle.

en.title: Türkiye: industrial scale, monetary disinflation and strategic autonomy between Europe and Asia
en.deck: Türkiye combines deep manufacturing, low sovereign debt and strategic geography with still-high inflation, external energy dependence and an unfinished shift toward higher-technology production; the central test is whether current disinflation becomes a durable institutional regime.
en.regime: Large transcontinental manufacturing economy undergoing restrictive disinflation, with low public debt and strong industrial capacity offset by high nominal instability, energy import dependence and large external financing flows.
en.key_risk: Premature monetary easing or a regional energy shock could restart the inflation-lira cycle before expectations and reserves are strong enough to sustain lower inflation.

publication.selection_rationale: Türkiye is a major NATO, Black Sea, Mediterranean and Middle Eastern actor with deep EU manufacturing integration, yet the public corpus lacked a reusable country dossier connecting its inflation and exchange-rate regime, manufacturing structure, energy dependence, defence industry, refugee system, earthquake reconstruction and strategic geography. Existing Europe–Russia–Ukraine, Russia, Iran and Saudi Arabia research all require Turkish context to avoid reconstructing the same transmission mechanisms.
contrary_evidence: Inflation above 30% and recurring lira volatility support a macroeconomic-instability thesis, while low public debt, a functioning banking system, manufacturing exports and large tourism receipts argue against a sovereign or institutional-collapse narrative.
EU accession negotiations remain stalled, but the EU absorbs over two-fifths of Turkish goods exports and Customs Union cooperation continued to deepen in 2026.
Domestic gas, LNG infrastructure and renewables improve energy security, while natural-gas imports still represented roughly 95% of 2025 supply.

Defence exports above US$10 billion demonstrate significant industrial capability, but export value does not establish full technological autonomy because imported components and foreign certifications remain relevant.
limitations: Inflation and growth forecasts changed materially during 2026 and must be attributed to their forecast date rather than averaged.
Turkish official sources are primary for administrative, trade, energy and defence-industry quantities but do not provide independent evaluation of policy performance.
Refugee stocks change through registration, voluntary return, resettlement and status changes; the latest UNHCR headline total used here is a mid-2025 snapshot.
Ethnicity is not comprehensively measured in official statistics, so the dossier avoids unsupported estimates of Kurdish or other ethnic population shares.
Defence-export figures are not equivalent to domestic value added or independently verified technological content.
Akkuyu's first unit remained in commissioning preparation at the evidence cutoff; planned generation is not counted as realised power supply.
Revision 1 adds the required evidence-bearing geographic map in both locales with semantic parity; no substantive factual conclusion is changed.
